🗃 SharePoint List Backend

✓ in syncSynced 8:52:13 am

Use your SharePoint list as the live database. Paste the two Power Automate HTTP flow URLs below — the portal reads the list on load and writes edits straight back.

✓ Loaded 31 service row(s).
📖 How to create the two flows
  1. READ: Power Automate → New → Instant cloud flow → trigger When an HTTP request is received.
  2. Add SharePoint → Get items. Point it at your site and list. Open Settings on that action and turn Pagination on with threshold 5000 — without it you only get the first 100 rows.
  3. Add a Response action: status 200, header Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, body body('Get_items')?['value'].
  4. Save, reopen the trigger, copy the generated URL into READ flow URL above.
  5. WRITE (optional): a second HTTP-triggered flow with a Condition on spId > 0 → Update item if yes, Create item if no. Copy its POST URL into WRITE flow URL.

Why flows and not the SharePoint API? The portal runs from file://, so its origin is null. Browsers won't send your Microsoft 365 cookies from a null origin and you can't register a file:// redirect URI for an Azure AD app, so a direct API call can never authenticate. The flow URL's signature is the credential instead.

⚠ Treat both URLs as passwords. Anyone holding them can read and write the list. Keep this file internal; if a URL leaks, resubmit the flow trigger to regenerate it.

Conversions handled for you: the eight progress/RAG columns are stored as whole percentages in SharePoint (99.3) but as fractions in the portal (0.993), so they are divided by 100 on load and multiplied back on save. Column names are matched loosely, so the display name, SharePoint's _x0020_ internal name, or the portal's own key all work.

🔔 Teams Webhook

Configured

✅ Pre-configured Power Automate webhook is already embedded. You can override it below if needed, or click ↻ Reset to Default to restore the built-in URL.

📖 How to create an Incoming Webhook in Teams
  1. Open Microsoft Teams → go to the target channel.
  2. Click ⋯ (More options) beside the channel name → Manage channel → Connectors.
    (Or select Workflows → template "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received".)
  3. Search for Incoming Webhook → click Configure.
  4. Enter a name (e.g. CSFC Transition Alerts) and optionally upload an icon.
  5. Click Create → copy the generated URL.
  6. Paste it above and click 💾 Save, then 🚨 Test Alert to verify.
💡 Alerts are triggered manually from this panel or automatically whenever a project transitions into < 40% RAG.

📅 Weekly Teams Summary

Enabled

No server/scheduler needed; the portal checks on load and self-guards against duplicate sends.

💡 Security notes
  • Password is hashed with salted SHA-256 (16-byte random salt). Plaintext never touches the file.
  • Login is rate-limited: 5 failed attempts in 60 s locks the form for 30 s.
  • Session auto-expires after 30 minutes of inactivity (mouse/key/click resets the timer).
  • Recommended: rotate the password every 90 days using the Change Password utility.

💡 Tips for near-zero-click distribution
  • Set your browser's default Downloads folder to a OneDrive-synced folder. The published HTML auto-syncs to the cloud and your team sees updates instantly.
  • Chrome/Edge (Chromium 86+): the "Smart Save" dialog remembers the folder you picked last — the second publish is a 1-click confirmation.
  • Use the "Latest (overwrite)" pattern (Dashboard_latest.html) if you want a stable filename your team can bookmark or link to.
  • Firefox: use about:preferences → General → Downloads → Always ask you where to save files to see a folder picker each time.
